title: Robot Scientist Eve Autonomously Discovers Triclosan Selectively Inhibits Malaria-Causing Plasmodium DHFR
aiSystem: Robot Scientist Eve (Econometric Active-Learning + QSAR Lab)
whyItMatters: Closed-loop AI robotic laboratory Eve autonomously designed assays, ran active-learning QSAR cycles, and discovered that triclosan selectively inhibits wild-type and pyrimethamine-resistant malaria DHFR enzymes.
summary: Published in the Journal of the Royal Society Interface on February 4, 2015 (with detailed enzymatic and molecular-mechanism follow-up in Scientific Reports, January 2018), Kevin Williams, Elizabeth Bilsland, Ross D. King, and collaborators at Cambridge, Manchester, and Aberystwyth deployed Robot Scientist Eve to automate early-stage neglected-disease drug discovery. Combining econometric active learning, symbolic/QSAR hypothesis generation, and robotic liquid-handling yeast assays, Eve autonomously screened compound libraries and discovered that the common antimicrobial triclosan selectively inhibits Plasmodium falciparum and P. vivax dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR)—including strains resistant to the frontline antimalarial pyrimethamine.
technicalHighlights: Executed closed-loop automated hypothesis generation, cherry-picking, assay execution, and econometric active learning over >1,400 compounds.
Autonomously discovered and experimentally verified triclosan as a selective inhibitor of both wild-type and pyrimethamine-resistant malaria DHFR.
Demonstrated substantial cost and assay reduction over brute-force high-throughput screening for neglected tropical diseases.
caveats: Identified a repurposed lead compound and mechanism in yeast/enzymatic assays rather than a clinically approved malaria therapeutic.

scoreRationale.foundational: First autonomous closed-loop robotic AI scientist to discover a validated anti-parasitic drug-target mechanism.
scoreRationale.ripple: Bridged symbolic Robot Scientist Adam to modern AI-driven self-driving wet labs (Coscientist, A-Lab).
scoreRationale.verification: Peer-reviewed in J. R. Soc. Interface (2015) and confirmed by enzymatic/crystallographic assays in Scientific Reports (2018).
scoreRationale.velocity: Active-learning experimental selection sharply cut screening cost and assay volume.
